title: SLO alignment bridge: playfest manual & integration tasks
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic playfest manual to run a cross-pillar SLO alignment and integration week (the "Playfest") for feature teams, platform, SRE and DS. Goal is to reduce SLO onboarding friction, validate telemetry handoffs, and leave participating teams with an actionable SLO + alert + runbook bundle for their primary service.

Context / why now:
- We keep getting partial SLOs that lack runbooks or realistic error budgets.
- Platform has new metric exporters (kafka -> metrics-proxy) and teams need a hands-on shop to wire things end-to-end.
- Want to accelerate reliable model-serving launches with a repeatable ritual instead of ad-hoc support.

Audience:
- Feature team leads and engineers (owner-level)
- Platform engineers + observability engineers
- SRE oncall leads and rotation owners
- Solutions/SEs for Dedicated/Private customers (to catch product-specific constraints)

High-level objectives (success criteria):
1) Each participating service ships a minimally-viable SLO doc + alert rule + 1-step runbook by end of Playfest.
2) 80% of telemetry gaps identified, prioritized and triaged into backlog tickets.
3) Platform-side exporter quirks for 3 top model-serving patterns identified and mitigations documented.
4) Create a canonical SLO checklist template and short demo used for future onboarding.

Scope (what we will and will not do):
- In scope: SLO definition, signal discovery, alert rule authoring, simple runbook creation, dashboard quickchecks, basic traffic/test plans for error budget exercises.
- Out of scope: full-scale chaos testing, deep perf tuning, contractual SLA negotiations (enterprise legal).

Week plan (example 5-day Playfest):
Day 0 (pre-work, 1 week prior):
- Teams register service, attach owner & oncall contacts to the Playfest sheet.
- Platform validates metric availability and flags missing dimensions.
- Pre-read: 1-pager + template sent to team owners.

Day 1: Align + discovery (half-day in-person or virtual)
- 09:00 intro, objectives, success criteria (Priya)
- 09:30 demo: canonical SLO flow (metric -> rule -> dashboard -> runbook) (Liam)
- 10:15 breakout: signal inventory for each service (teams)
- 15:00 sync: list of missing metrics + quick fixes (platform)

Day 2: Authoring + wiring (hands-on)
- Morning: pair platform + team to wire exporters and metric tags
- Afternoon: draft SLO doc and alert rules in staging monitoring project

Day 3: Runbooks + canary plans
- Morning: write 1-page runbook + escalation path, owner signs off
- Afternoon: choose simple canary failure scenarios, prepare test harness

Day 4: Error budget exercise + ops rehearsal
- Run small simulated incidents to exercise runbooks, capture gaps
- Update alerts/dashboards based on rehearsal outcomes

Day 5: Wrap + backlog grooming + launch checklist
- Final sign-off on each service bundle
- Triage follow-ups into JIRA board and assign owners
- Retro + lessons learned, publish canonical checklist to Confluence

Roles & responsibilities (rough):
- Playfest lead: Priya Nair — overall schedule, stakeholder nudges, final sign-off
- Platform eng lead: Liam Chen — exporter fixes, quick patches, staging infra
- Observability SME: Sofia Martinez — alert rule templates, dashboard pruning
- SRE liaison: Evan Brooks — runbook templates, incident rehearsal design
- Customer/SE observer: Aisha Rahman — surface customer constraints (Dedicated/Private)
- Team owners: TBD per service — bring context, accept runbook/alert responsibilities

Artifacts to produce per-service (minimum):
- service-slo.md (1 page with objective, SLI definitions, target, measurement window)
- alert-rules.yml (in staging-monitoring repo path)
- runbook-<service>.md (1 page: detection -> immediate mitigation -> escalate -> postmortem triggers)
- canary-test-plan.md (2-3 steps to simulate typical failure)

Measurement & post-Playfest follow-up:
- Baseline telemetry coverage spreadsheet (pre/post) to measure lift
- Triage JIRA board with three priority lanes: P0 (blocked launches), P1 (missing metrics), P2 (nice-to-have dashboards)
- 30/60/90 day check-ins: automated reminders to owners to confirm SLOs held, and change requests funneled via SLO RFC process

Communications and stakeholder plan:
- Pre-playfest: invite calendar + short pre-read 7 days before (owner: Priya)
- Daily standups (15m) during Playfest for cross-team unblock (channel #ops-slo-onboarding)
- Final report + artifact links published to Confluence and announced in #eng-all

Risk & mitigations (quick):
- Risk: Platform exporter bugs block a team's ability to measure SLI.
  Mitigation: Feature a fallback synthetic SLI and escalate a hotfix patch in staging.
- Risk: Teams over-scope and try to finish too many services.
  Mitigation: Cap to 6 services per Playfest; prioritize highest-impact launches.
- Risk: Oncall owners unavailable for rehearsal.
  Mitigation: Schedule rehearsals early in day, allow oncall proxies, require owner sign-off asynchronously if necessary.

Pre-Playfest checklist (owners in parens):
- Register service and owner in Playfest sheet (team owner)
- Confirm basic metrics exist for the last 7 days (platform + owner)
- Provide stub monitoring project access (platform)
- Run quick smoke to collect 1000 requests sample for latency/error SLIs (team owner)

Runbook template (short):
- Title & scope
- Symptoms that indicate this runbook applies
- Immediate mitigation steps (3 bullets)
- Stateful checks to run (metrics/queries)
- Escalation path (pager + Slack channel)
- Postmortem criteria and owner

Ops rehearsal script (30 min):
- Trigger synthetic 10% error spike for 10 minutes in staging
- Verify alert fires within expected window
- Execute runbook mitigation step 1, observe outcomes
- Escalate to oncall and test paging path
- Record timings and gaps

Open questions / tradeoffs (items to resolve before run):
- Metric cardinality limits: do we standardize SLI label set for model-serving? (UX vs cost)
- Error budget policy: do we allow temporary 'grace windows' during major infra upgrades?
- Should SLO ownership be a hard gating for production promotion in CI? pros/cons noted in playfest retro.

Next steps (immediate):
- Finalize participant list by 2026-05-07 (Priya)
- Run platform export readiness scan by 2026-05-09 (Liam)
- Share pre-read + template to teams 2026-05-10 (Sofia)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep exercises concrete and short; teams bail if too theory-heavy.
- Build one canned demo that shows metric -> alert -> page in 12 steps.
- Capture video of a successful rehearsal; can be a reusable onboarding asset.

Attachments to create after Playfest:
- canonical-slo-checklist.md
- sla-vs-slo-one-pager
- recordings + short clips of runbook rehearsal

— end of manual —

Revision log:
- 2026-05-03 initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-05-06 added week plan and roles (Liam, Sofia)
- 2026-05-12 updated risk mitigations and playfest limits after sync with SRE (Evan)
